title: Zippered surge fragility — ephemeral backlog probe
content:
Purpose:
Quick notes from a lightweight experiment probing an asymmetric "zippered" surge pattern that alternates short high-intensity bursts across two ingress streams (A and B) out of phase. Trying to reproduce a class of tail spikes we see in production where aggregate Q depth oscillates even when average QPS is within SLO headroom.

Hypothesis:
When two independent traffic lanes send short, overlapping microbursts in anti-phase (zipper), shared KV-cache priming + scheduler slot exhaustion produces high p99.9 amplification due to transient queue reordering and head-of-line blocking. Preemption and burst-coalescing behaviors interact poorly.

Environment & config:
- Cluster: 4 nodes (p4d-like sim) locally; 8 CPU workers for load gen, isolated runtime binary from feature/ingress-zippers branch.
- Model: small open LLM (seq 1024) quantized dynamic; KV cache enabled.
- Scheduler: default fair-queue slots (slot-size=8), concurrency limit 64 per instance.
- Traffic generator: custom harness (node) that emits zippered pattern: stream A emits 120 reqs at 300 qps for 0.4s every 3s; stream B emits same but delayed by 1.5s. Background steady traffic 50 qps.
- Measurement: per-request timestamps, queue depth, KV cache hit-rate, token generation time.

Run notes (abridged):
1) Baseline (no zipper, constant 200 qps): median=85ms, p95=200ms, p99=410ms, p99.9=880ms. KV hit-rate steady ~93%.
2) Zipper pattern (A/B anti-phase): median=98ms, p95=240ms, p99=630ms, p99.9=2.34s (spike clusters aligned with overlap windows). Queue depth traces show sawtooth with amplitude 2.5x baseline during overlap windows.
3) Disable KV priming (cold cache for each request): p99.9 worsens to ~3.1s, but interestingly p50 barely moves — indicates KV interactions matter for tails.
4) Enable preemptive-short-job-priority (experimental): p99.9 drops to 1.6s but p95 increases slightly; observed more request requeues.

Observations & quick interpretations:
- Overlap windows create local bursts that temporarily starve scheduler slot pool; short requests that would normally finish act as resource hogs when their KV priming forces longer token stalls.
- Cache priming behavior amplifies fragility: first requests in overlap often perform the bulk of costly KV warming which stalls other in-flight work (shared CPU/GPU stage contention).
- Preemption helps long-tail but at cost of increased median due to requeue overhead; suggests tunable threshold trade-offs.
- Simple autoscale (scale on avg qps) is blind to these micro-overlaps; autoscale trigger lag can make things worse.

Quick reproduction steps (local):
- checkout feature/ingress-zippers, make run-harness
- config: scheduler.slot_size=8, concurrency=64, kv_cache.enabled=true
- start runtime: ./bin/runtime --workers=4 --metrics-port=9090
- load gen: node tools/zipper-gen.js --a-peak=300 --a-window=0.4 --b-delay=1.5 --duration=600
- collect traces: curl localhost:9090/metrics; tail /var/log/runtime/requests.log | jq -c .

Diagnostics to capture next time:
- Per-core CPU sleep/wakeup patterns during overlap (maybe de-sched interactions).
- GPU queueing backlog from host->device DMA during first-token stalls.
- Fine-grained KV backend timings (single-key latencies) and eviction rate correlations.
- Instrument scheduler slot assignment order to see if ordering correlates with large token stalls.

Immediate mitigation ideas to A/B:
- Conservative burst-coalescing: delay accepting ephemeral spikes for 50–100ms to smooth overlap; measure effect on p50/p99.
- Adaptive preemption: only preempt when estimated remaining tokens > X and when queue depth > Y.
- KV priming isolation: run KV priming work in bounded worker pool to avoid stalling inference worker threads.
- Admission control by lane: limit simultaneous requests accepted from each ingress lane during overlap windows.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we synthesize the same p99.9 behavior with purely Poisson aggregated load? (probably not; zipper-specific.)
- What is the true cost of preemption on downstream correctness/ordering semantics for streaming?
- How much of the effect is infra (CPU/GPU contention) vs. software ordering? Need perf counters.
- Schedule a short run with real production traces replayed in zipper alignment (ask SRE for sample segment).

Attachments / artifacts to add once available:
- heatmaps of queue depth over time (png)
- per-request waterfall for a representative overlap window (har)
- CPU/gpu perf counters (flamegraphs)

Notes to self:
- Keep this short: goal is to decide whether to treat zipper-class overlap as new SLO break pattern and add a targeted mitigation to the scheduler.
- Ping Omar for perf-counter hooks, Riley for load-gen tuning, Maya for KV backend trace access.

Sign-off: Anika P. (quick scratchpad, not a runbook).
short_summary: Scratchpad for a local experiment that reproduces p99.9 amplification under an anti-phase \"zippered\" ingress pattern. Tests show KV priming + scheduler slot exhaustion amplify tails; preemption helps tail but raises median. Next steps: perf counters and targeted mitigations.
